claim: Israel's government speaks for all Israelis (and its mirror: all Israelis are the same).

heard.quote: I intend to be the prime minister of all," he said Sunday. "Of those who elected me, and of those who did not elect me.

answer: Israel's 120-seat Knesset is elected by pure proportional vote in one national district, with a 3.25% threshold, so no party has ever won a majority and every government is a coalition. Small parties therefore carry real weight. The November 2022 election produced a government of Likud, two ultra-Orthodox parties and the Religious Zionism and Otzma Yehudit list; Yesh Atid, National Unity, Yisrael Beiteinu, Labor and two Arab-majority lists sat in opposition. The camps differ on a Palestinian state, from the Democrats' opposition to annexation to the coalition's claim of an exclusive Jewish right to the whole land, and on religion and state. Ra'am sat in the 2021 to 2022 coalition. The October 2026 election gave no bloc 61 seats.

facts.text: The Knesset has 120 seats, is elected by proportional representation in one nationwide district, and a list needs at least 3.25% of valid votes to win seats.

sources.title: Country Profile: Israel
sources.quote: There is a 3.25% threshold required to gain representation. All candidates run in one, nationwide district.

sources.title: EXPLAINER - How Israel's election system works
sources.quote: Israel uses nationwide proportional representation, with the entire country treated as a single electoral district.

sources.title: Live 2026 Israel election results
sources.quote: parties must receive at least 3.25% of the vote to enter the Knesset, equivalent to a minimum of four seats.

facts.text: No party has ever won 61 seats, so every government is a coalition, which gives small parties leverage: a faction just under or over the threshold can change which bloc governs.

sources.title: Israel's Political System
sources.quote: since no single party has ever won a majority of the seats in the Knesset, this requires forming a coalition with other parties in order to win majority approval.

sources.title: Israel's Political System
sources.quote: smaller parties often represent the additional votes needed to pass legislation.

sources.title: EXPLAINER - How Israel's election system works
sources.quote: The threshold makes smaller parties particularly important.

sources.title: Live 2026 Israel election results
sources.quote: Parties need 61 seats to secure a majority and form a government in Israel.

facts.text: The November 2022 election (the 25th Knesset) gave Likud 32 seats, Yesh Atid 24, Religious Zionism with Otzma Yehudit and Noam 14, National Unity 12, Shas 11, United Torah Judaism 7, Yisrael Beiteinu 6, Ra'am 5, Hadash-Ta'al 5 and Labor 4; Meretz and Balad fell under the threshold.

facts.text: Likud descends from the Revisionist movement of Jabotinsky through Herut (founded 1948), joined the Likud bloc in 1973, and under Menachem Begin won the 1977 election that ended Labor's rule.

sources.title: Likud
sources.quote: the Herut had its roots in Vladimir Jabotinsky 's Revisionist Zionism , popular especially among Russian Jews of the 1920s and '30s.

sources.title: Israel - The Likud Bloc
sources.quote: In the ninth Knesset elections in May 1977, the center-right Likud alliance emerged victorious and replaced the previously dominant Labor alignment

sources.title: Likud
sources.quote: headed by Menachem Begin, Likud first came to power in 1977 and continued as the ruling party until 1984.

facts.text: On the Palestinian question the Likud-led government that took office in December 2022 declared in its guidelines that the Jewish people have an exclusive and indisputable right to all parts of the Land of Israel, while promising to keep the religion-and-state status quo.

sources.quote: Its founding documents state unequivocally that the Jewish people have an "exclusive and indisputable right to all parts of the Land of Israel"

facts.text: The Labor movement ran Israel from 1948: Mapai was the dominant party, every prime minister until 1977 came from it or its successor Labor, and Labor's line moved to support a Palestinian state; it merged with Meretz in 2024 into The Democrats.

sources.title: Labor Party (Ha'avoda)
sources.quote: on the issue of the Israeli-Palestinian conflict, the party gradually moved to the left over the years and was the first major party to call for negotiations with the PLO and to support the establishment of a Palestinian state.

sources.title: Labor and Meretz merge into united 'liberal-democratic Zionist party': The Democrats
sources.quote: Newly elected Labor chairman Yair Golan largely fulfilled his pledge to unify Israel's liberal camp on Sunday, announcing a merger with the left-wing Meretz

sources.title: The Democrats
sources.quote: The Democrats is an electoral list that was founded in 2024 as a result of a merger between the Labor Party and Meretz

facts.text: The Democrats' published principles include halting the annexation process in the West Bank, amending the nation-state law in the spirit of the Declaration of Independence, civil marriage and limited public transport on Shabbat.

sources.title: The Democrats
sources.quote: religion and state: promote the operation of public transport on Shabbat in a limited format in secular localities; promote civil marriage

sources.title: Labor and Meretz merge into united 'liberal-democratic Zionist party': The Democrats
sources.quote: a liberal-democratic Zionist party that will be a political home for a large part of the Israeli population

facts.text: The centre: Yesh Atid calls itself a centrist liberal party focused on civic issues, and its leader Yair Lapid, as prime minister in 2022, told the UN that a deal based on two states for two peoples is the right thing for Israel, on condition the Palestinian state is peaceful.

sources.title: Yesh Atid
sources.quote: Yesh Atid positions itself as a centrist liberal party and its platform focuses largely on social and civic issues and governance, and less on defense and foreign affairs.

sources.title: Israeli Prime Minister Lapid backs two-State solution
sources.quote: a large majority of Israelis support the vision of this two-State solution. I am one of them

facts.text: The religious-Zionist right: Religious Zionism is placed on the far right by the IDI, advocates the Greater Land of Israel with expanded West Bank settlement, and seeks to limit the Supreme Court; it ran in 2022 on a joint list with Otzma Yehudit and Noam.

sources.title: Religious Zionist Party
sources.quote: it advocates the principle the "Greater Land of Israel" (supports the expansion of settlement projects in the West Bank / Judea and Samaria), and calls for an aggressive defense policy.

sources.title: Israel Election Final Results
sources.quote: followed by the far-right Religious Zionism - headed by Bezalel Smotrich and Kahanist lawmaker Itamar Ben-Gvir

facts.text: Otzma Yehudit has Kahanist roots: its figures come from the movement of Rabbi Meir Kahane, whose Kach party was barred from the Knesset elections in 1988 after Israel's parliament amended the election law against incitement to racism.

sources.title: Otzma Yehudit
sources.quote: its organizational roots can be traced back to the Jewish National Front, a party founded in 2004 by Baruch Marzel

sources.title: Kahane's ghost: how a long-dead extremist rabbi continues to haunt Israel's politics
sources.quote: Kach was banned from running in the 1988 elections and the supreme court rejected Kahane's appeal.

sources.title: Otzma Yehudit's history of racism and provocation
sources.quote: but its roots are in the Kach movement, which Kahane established in the 1970s.

facts.text: Kach was disqualified from the 1988 election, and after 1994 Kach and Kahane Chai were declared terrorist organisations in Israel.

sources.title: Kach Party
sources.quote: In the 1988 elections for the 12th Knesset, Kach was indeed disqualified from running.

sources.title: Kahane's ghost: how a long-dead extremist rabbi continues to haunt Israel's politics
sources.quote: In 1985, Israel's parliament passed a bill that amended the country's basic law to bar any party or politician that supports violent terrorism

sources.title: Otzma Yehudit's history of racism and provocation
sources.quote: In response, all of the parliament's factions came together to pass a law forbidding parties that incite to racism from running in the elections.

facts.text: The ultra-Orthodox parties: Shas, founded in 1984 by Sephardic haredim, backs peace deals that preserve security but opposes dividing Jerusalem, and United Torah Judaism, a list of Agudat Israel and Degel HaTorah, serves haredi education, welfare and army-service interests and tends to back the right because it is conservative on religion.

sources.title: Shas
sources.quote: Shas supports arriving at peace agreements with the Arab states while preserving the security of the residents of Israel, but is opposed to the division of Jerusalem.

sources.title: United Torah Judaism
sources.quote: The party does tend to support the right-wing camp, however, because that camp tends to have a more conservative outlook on religious issues.

sources.title: What 'right' and 'left' mean in Israel today
sources.quote: Shas and United Torah Judaism are conservative on religion, family, gender roles and the public place of Judaism.

facts.text: Yisrael Beiteinu, founded by Avigdor Liberman in 1999 for immigrants from the former Soviet Union, combines hawkish positions on the Palestinians (population exchanges and two ethnically homogeneous states) with secular positions on religion and state, including universal conscription.

sources.title: Yisrael Beitenu
sources.quote: the party's proposed solution for the conflict with the Palestinians is based upon population exchanges and the creation of two ethnically homogeneous states.

sources.title: What does Avigdor Liberman's Yisrael Beytenu stand for?
sources.quote: sits on the right of the political aisle on security and national issues but leans secular-liberal on matters of religion and state.

facts.text: Ra'am, an Islamist-rooted Arab party, joined the Bennett-Lapid coalition in June 2021, the first time an independent Arab party sat in an Israeli government; it supports a Palestinian state with Jerusalem as its capital and recognition of Arab citizens as a national minority.

sources.title: Ra'am
sources.quote: following the 2021 Ra'am joined the coalition supporting the Bennett-Lapid government. That was the first time an Arab party was a formal member of the governing coalition.

sources.title: History made as Arab Israeli Ra'am party joins Bennett-Lapid coalition
sources.quote: This is the first time that an Arab party is part of the process of forming a government.

sources.title: The Arab Kingmaker Who Joined Israel's Far-Right to Oust Netanyahu
sources.quote: a devout Muslim and Palestinian citizen of Israel into a coalition government with the two Jewish Zionist leaders

facts.text: The other Arab-majority lists differ from Ra'am: Hadash, a mixed Arab-Jewish list with communist roots, was among the first parties to champion two states, and Balad seeks a state of all its citizens; Balad fell under the threshold in 2022.

sources.title: Hadash
sources.quote: Hadash had a distinct communist orientation and was among the first parties in Israel to champion the idea of two states for two peoples

sources.title: Balad
sources.quote: it champions turning the state of Israel into a "state of all of its citizens."

sources.title: Israel Election Final Results
sources.quote: Arab nationalist party Balad and Ayelet Shaked's Habayit Hayehudi failed to make it into the Knesset.

contested.text: Whether to call the ultra-Orthodox parties right-wing: the IDI calls United Torah Judaism centrist on foreign policy and says it leans right because of religious conservatism, and a 2026 analysis says their coalition choices are driven by budgets and religious autonomy more than by the Palestinians.

sources.title: United Torah Judaism
sources.quote: regarding foreign policy and security, United Torah Judaism is a centrist party, which determines its positions based on religious concerns more than security concerns or diplomatic considerations.

sources.title: What 'right' and 'left' mean in Israel today
sources.quote: Coalition choices are driven less by a fixed position on the Palestinians than by budgets, education, religious autonomy and military exemptions.

contested.text: How to describe Religious Zionism: the IDI places it on the far right, and Haaretz calls the list far-right with a Kahanist lawmaker; the list's own platform stresses Jewish identity and the Greater Land of Israel.

sources.title: Religious Zionist Party
sources.quote: ideologically, the Religious Zionist Party is located on the far right of the political map.

sources.title: Israel Election Final Results
sources.quote: followed by the far-right Religious Zionism - headed by Bezalel Smotrich and Kahanist lawmaker Itamar Ben-Gvir

Whether a 26th-Knesset government has formed. The brief named the 2022 Knesset as current. Another agent reported no official 2026 results; the checker's fetch does read votes26.bechirot.gov.il (Central Elections Committee, 27 October 2026 election, 11 lists, Likud 27), a Reuters results graphic, the IDI party pages and a Midbar report, so the results stay on the card; a government is not yet reported.

A third independent source for several single-camp facts (Hadash and Balad platforms; Shas and United Torah Judaism; Yisrael Beiteinu on a Palestinian state; Religious Zionism's platform): the IDI party pages are one site.

A readable source for Otzma Yehudit's stated aims (death penalty for terrorists, Jewish law in the judicial system): only the IDI page was readable, so that fact was removed; the Tony Blair Institute page that carries the 2019 platform blocked the checker.
A Times of Israel Lapid speech page and the Reuters 2022 mandate story: neither was readable; the Lapid fact rests on the IDI and the UN News report.

not_claimed: That any party speaks for a whole community: Arab citizens, ultra-Orthodox, secular, settlers and others vote across many lists.
That the camps are monoliths or that a party's platform equals its voters' views.
That one camp is more legitimate than another.
That describing a party's roots means every member shares the founders' positions.
